summary: Geoffrey Hinton, a pioneer in artificial intelligence, quit Google to speak freely about the dangers of AI, including the risk that computers could become smarter than humans sooner than expected. He expressed concerns about AI's ability to create convincing false content and displace workers, and called for regulation.

claims.text: Geoffrey Hinton quit Google to speak freely about AI dangers without considering how it impacts Google.
claims.evidence_quote: I left so that I could talk about the dangers of AI without considering how this impacts Google

claims.text: Hinton is worried about AI's capacity to create convincing false images and texts, making it hard to know what is true.
claims.evidence_quote: not be able to know what is true anymore

claims.text: Hinton believes AI could become smarter than people sooner than expected, contrary to his earlier estimate of 30 to 50 years.
claims.evidence_quote: I thought it was 30 to 50 years or even longer away. Obviously, I no longer think that.

claims.text: Hinton said Google acted responsibly and denied quitting to criticize his former employer.
claims.evidence_quote: Google itself had 'acted very responsibly' and denied that he had quit so that he could criticise his former employer.

claims.text: Google's chief scientist Jeff Dean stated the company remains committed to a responsible approach to AI.
claims.evidence_quote: We remain committed to a responsible approach to A.I. We’re continually learning to understand emerging risks while also innovating boldly.

claims.text: The release of ChatGPT by OpenAI in November has increased concerns about generative AI and its regulation.
claims.evidence_quote: Since Microsoft-backed startup OpenAI released ChatGPT in November, the growing number of 'generative AI' applications that can create text or images have provoked concern over the future regulation of the technology.

claims.text: Dr. Carissa Veliz, an associate professor at Oxford, said the time to regulate AI is now.
claims.evidence_quote: The time to regulate AI is now.

claims.text: Hinton warned that AI could quickly displace workers and become a greater danger as it learns new behaviors.
claims.evidence_quote: The technology could quickly displace workers, and become a greater danger as it learns new behaviours.
